overview_markdown:
MicroClaw is a self-hosted agentic AI platform written in Rust, inspired by nanoclaw and positioned as a lightweight alternative in the OpenClaw ecosystem. Its architecture centers on a single embeddable agent core that powers three surfaces: **MicroClaw Server** for always-on chat channels, APIs, scheduling, and automation; **MicroClaw Work**, a native GPUI desktop app for local workspace-centered agent sessions; and **`microclaw-sdk`**, which lets other Rust applications embed the same channel-independent Agent Engine with tools, policy, memory, skills, and runtime events.

The project is designed for work that outlasts a single request: multi-step tool use, resumable sessions, durable delivery, persistent memory, scheduled tasks, and governed extensions all run in one runtime. Compared to OpenClaw, MicroClaw trades ecosystem breadth for a lean Rust foundation, a native desktop experience, and an SDK-first embedding story. Development is active — the v0.6.1 release shipped recently with SDK 0.5.1 adding skill and delegation APIs — though the maintainers caution that `main` moves fast and production users should pin to the `stable` branch.
